title: 2006 AMC 10A Problem 21
statement: How many four-digit positive integers have at least one digit that is a \(2\) or a \(3?\)

solutions.text:
There are \(9000\) four-digit integers. For those avoiding \(2\) and \(3,\) the leading digit is one of \(\{1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}\) (\(7\) choices) and each remaining digit is one of \(\{0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}\) (\(8\) choices): \(7 \cdot 8^3 = 3584.\)

So \(9000 - 3584 = 5416\) have at least one \(2\) or \(3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Count the complement: four-digit numbers with no \(2\) and no \(3\)
The leading digit has \(7\) choices; each other digit has \(8\)
